A user can initiate data entry of a new Rx via following:

Main Menu or Patient Profile: System shall continue processing through FARx.DE.01.01

Triage Queue (QT) / Drive Thru Queue (QD): System shall continue processing through FARx.DE.01.235 *


User selects Process Hard Copy Request of a new prescription Hard Copy Request Detail screen (Hard Copy Request was created on a prescription-fill = 00)* (Refer to DE.01.366)


User selects Process Diagnosis Code Request of a new prescription Diagnosis Code Detail screen (Diagnosis Code Request was created on a prescription-fill = 00)* (Refer to DE.01.514)


User selects to create a new prescription for TP Plan Benefit Consult Request*: System shall continue processing through DE.01 – Flow 11


User selects to Edit from an Auto Process Error Exception due to Missing Data Entry Fields: System shall continue to DE.01.1202
User selects to continue from Savings Finder – MFR Coupon Screen for an On-Hold prescription :System shall continue to DE.01.1775
User selects to Continue from Savings Finder – Fill Selected Drug Screen for an On-Hold Prescription : System shall continue to DE.01.1776
User selects to Continue from Savings Finder – Discount Card Screen for an On-Hold Prescription : System shall continue to DE.01.1177
User selects “New Rx” from the PCC detailed view -System shall continue to DE.01.2095
User selects “Vaccine Clinic Data Entry (V)” from main menu, selects a Vaccine and a Patient from Vaccine Clinic Details screen and then continues to New Rx Screen. (as a part of Vaccine Clinic Process)
System shall continue from Alternate Flow 20.

User selects to Fill an Immunization Gap from Immunization Profile.
System shall continue to Alternate Flow 24.

User navigates to Data Entry from "New Rx - Immunization Request" item opened from QT.
System shall continue to Alternate Flow 24.

* Note: New Rx data entry not available during offline thru Triage Queue / Drive Thru Queue or Process Hard Copy Request, Process Diagnosis Code Request, or TP Plan Benefit Consult Request

If user selects to fill a new Rx via Main Menu or Patient Profile, the user must perform the following:

Search and select the patient in the system. If the desired patient is not found in the system, the user can add the patient in the system and proceed. Refer Functional Activity Document FARx.PA.00 Search Patient and FARx.PA.02 Patient Add.
On selecting the patient, the system shall display the Standard Patient Header (Refer to FARx.PA.01.18)
Data Entry fields as per Alternate Flow 26

If the user selects to fill a ‘New Rx’ via Triage Queue, the system shall display “New Prescription” screen for data entry with
Standard Patient Header (Refer to FARx.PA.01.18)
Data Entry fields as per Alternate Flow 4

If the user selects to fill a ‘New Rx’ via selecting ‘Process Hard Copy Request’, the system shall display “New Prescription” screen for data entry with
Standard Patient Header (Refer to FARx.PA.01.18)
Data Entry fields as per Alternate Flow 6

If the user selects to fill a ‘New Rx’ via selecting ‘Process Diagnosis Code Request’ (Refer to FARx.QR.22.05), the system shall display “New Prescription” screen for data entry with
Standard Patient Header (Refer to FARx.PA.01.18)
Data Entry fields as per Alternate Flow 6

If the user selects to fill a ‘New Rx’ via Auto Process Exception due to Missing Data Entry Fields, the system shall display “New Prescription” screen for data entry with
Standard Patient Header (Refer to FARx.PA.01.18)
Data Entry fields as per DE.01.1200

If the user selects to fill a ‘New Rx’ via Prescriber Request Rejection, the system shall display “New Prescription” screen for data entry with
Standard Patient Header (Refer to FARx.PA.01.18)
If the system evaluates that the prescription is a waiter, the system displays an indicator of waiter per FARx.WI.01
Data Entry fields as per DE.01.1227

Verifying

When the user selects to create a new prescription for an enterprise patient, the system shall determine if the patient has been completely synched with enterprise services (i.e. the patient is not in a “pending enterprise” status – Refer to FARx.PA.02 Alternate Flow 7)
If the patient has been completely synched, the system shall continue from DE.01.1223
If the patient has NOT been completely synced, the system shall display the below message for 5 seconds
 “Please wait as the system attempts to synch the patient’s enterprise information”
After 5 seconds if enterprise synch is not achieved completely, system shall 
Close the above message 
Display the below message with a red border
“Enterprise patient synch was not successful.  Please note that the patient’s TP Information may not be correct.”
After 5 seconds if enterprise synch is successfully completely, system shall continue with data entry from DE.01.1223

The system shall display ‘Patient Alert Message’ (Refer to FARx.PAM.01) on top of the ‘Data Entry’ screen when ALL the following conditions are true:
Patient Alert Message Workflow Display (Refer to Corp Root App Option # 1431 – FAAM.AP.01b) is set to ‘New Rx’
An ‘Active’ patient alert Message is associated with the patient whose prescription(s) is being data entered (Refer to FAAM.PAM.01)
Data Entry is not initiated as a part of filling an Immunization gap (Refer FARx.IMM.10) or "New Rx - Immunization Request" QT item. (Refer FARx.QT.10)

When the user selects ‘Place On Hold’ on the Patient Alert Message screen during new manual Rx data entry and the following conditions are true:
If Enable Patient Level Alert 2.0 is set to ‘Yes’ (Refer to PAAM.PAM.01).
The ‘Bypass Fill’, ‘Do Not Fill’ and ‘Place On Hold’ fill options are available.
Patient Level Alert Message was identified during new Rx workflow (Refer to FARx.DE.01.1223)
User selects Place On Hold option and enters credentials from Patient Alert Message screen.
Then continue to FARx.DE.01.2852

The system shall display the On Hold data entry screen:
User completes On Hold data entry (Refer to Alternate Flow 1).
If user exits out of the On Hold workflow prior completion, then the system shall return the display to the originating screen.
The system shall place Rx On Hold upon successful credentialing.
If the new Rx data entry was initiated via action queue line item, then close the line item with disposition taken.
The system shall navigate to originating screen or next item if N-Key is enabled.
When Enable Patient Level Alert 2.0 is set to ‘No’ (Refer to FAAM.PAM.01) the system shall not invoke On Hold processing from Patient Alert prompt.

When the user selects to fill a new Rx via Main Menu or Patient Profile AND when the store is enabled to display top customer information (Refer to FAAM.TCB.01 Manage Top Customer Settings), the system shall check if the patient is a top customer
If the patient is a top customer, the system shall display the configurable top customer message specific to data entry. (Refer to FAAM.TCB.01 Manage Top Customer Settings)
NAVIGATION OPTION: Continue (Enter): closes the message dialog and proceed with DE.01.02
If the patient is not a top customer. The system shall not display the top customer messaging and proceed with DE.01.02

Display CEE “Action Item” indicator *
The system shall display an indicator on the data entry screen if open CEE opportunityies or a 90 Day Opportunity exist for the patient  

The system shall display the indicator if all of the following conditions are true:
At least one open CEE opportunity exists for the patient and the opportunity applies to the current store
At least one of the corresponding opportunity types for the associated open CEE opportunity/ies is Active (Refer to FAAM.CEE.01.03) AND
Is configured to “Display indication of open opportunity on Patient Profile or DE screen” (Refer Functional Activity Document FAAM.CEE.01.27 – Config 2)
If the opportunity is configured as category is “Add Therapy” and label delivery (i.e. Label Receipt and Forced Counseling is configured to 2 or 3) the following must also be true:
The Opportunity Status is ‘Printed’ and the Rx on which the opportunity is printed is Sold.
OR
If the following is true:
At least one open 90 Day opportunity exists for the patient and the opportunity applies to the current store (per FARx.CEE.03.130).

* These requirements shall not apply if the corporate root application option “Enable CEE” (Refer to FAAM.AP.01b – tab CORPORATE (Consolidated) – item # 261) is set to “Disabled” for the corresponding store
*The open action item indicator will not be displayed for the opportunities sent to Central PCC queue for processing, which includes Open CEE opportunities configured to display for the patient in the current store on the Data Entry screen and 90 Day opportunities. If the only items that are actionable for this patient are items that were sent to CPCC Queue for processing, then do not display an open action item indicator on the Data Entry screen.

If auto-substitution occurred, the system shall:

For the Substituted Product, the system shall identify all the product messages to be displayed during Drug Selection workflow step which are defined at the NDC level and all the inherited product messages from other sources (GCNSEQNO, HICL, HICSEQNO):
If there are no product messages identified to be displayed, the system shall not display Product Messages
If at-least one product message is identified to be displayed, the system shall determine if it needs to be displayed as Hard Stop or Soft Stop
If none of the Drug Selection Hard Stop checkbox (at NDC level and all other associated levels) is set as checked, the system shall display the messages as Soft Stop.
If at-least one of the Drug Selection Hard Stop checkboxes (at NDC level and any other associated levels) is set as checked, the system shall display the messages as Hard Stop.
The Product Messages shall be displayed on a message box with title as “Quality Alert”.
The Product Message text shall be displayed in the RED.
The “Quality Alert” message box shall be outlined with RED border.
The product messages should display as per the “Priority” assigned to each message by the Administrator user. Priority “1” on the top and Priority “4” at the bottom.

If to be displayed as Soft Stop
The system shall provide following navigation options on the “Quality Alert” dialog:
Continue I – Selecting this option the system shall close the “Quality Alert” message box and shall continue processing and the focus shall be on the next field.
Reselect (R) – Selecting this option the system shall close the “Quality Alert” message box and shall set the focus on the Drug field.

If to be displayed as Hard Stop
The system shall provide following navigation options on the “Quality Alert” dialog:
Enter / Scan Credentials – The pharmacy staff members shall be able to scan the credentials or enter credentials to continue. 
Once credentials are validated, the system shall 
Close the “Quality Alert” message box and shall continue processing.
The system shall capture and retain credentials for this action. The system shall maintain the workflow step at which the credentials were captured.
If invalid credentials are entered:
The product message shall disappear and an error message shall display indicating that incorrect credentials were entered.
The pharmacy staff members shall acknowledge the error message (presses Enter)
The error message shall disappear and the product message shall re-display requesting credentials to be entered.
Reselect (R) – Selecting this option will close the “Quality Alert” message box and shall set the focus on the Drug field.

Fills where no dispensable units are present: (e.g. tabs & caps)
Total Daily Dose =  
Dispensed Quantity/Days Supply

Fills where dispensable units is not null: (e.g. Inhalers)
Total Daily Dose= 
[(Dispensable Unit)*(Dispense Qty / Pack Size)] / Days Supply

Total Daily Dose shall be used for DUR dosing only.
The system shall automatically calculate the day’s supply on refills when the Dispense Quantity is updated or the dispensable units is present on a drug (e.g. inhalers). The system shall use the following calculation when determining the refill days supply:
Refills where no dispensable units are present:
Day’s Supply = 
Day’s Supply of Current Fill=Dispensed Quantity of Current Fill / Total Daily Dose from Previous Fill.

Refills where dispensable units is present:
Day’s Supply = 
[(Dispensable Units)*(Dispensed Qty of current fill/Pkg Size)]/ Total Daily Dose from Previous Fill.

The system shall set Anticipated PD&T to be System Time (Time when valid Credentials are entered) + ‘x’ mins (Refer to FAAM.AP.01b – Reg App option # 814)

The system shall follow existing Promise Date and Time rules for the above scenarios where the PD&T is systematically updated


Example:
Pharmacy open hours 9 AM to 6 PM 
A customer comes at  5:30 PM  for an Rx. on 09/08 
Corp adin setting for app option 'Set Promise Date and Time forRPh Review Exception items'  is 30 mins 
System time entered during Data Entry is 12 PM on 09/09 
Assuming that at 5:45 PM, user selected Send to RPh and credentials, so anticipated time for RPh Review Exception item becomes  5:45 PM +30 mins  = 6:15 PM
System compares 6:15 PM with Store close times i.e. 6PM and since anticipated time exceeds store close time, the system shall add the configurable time to the next day store open hours
So the anticipated PD&T = 9 AM  + 30 mins = 9:30 AM 09/09 
As per the Functional Activity Document, comparing the user entered time and the anticipated time, system shall set the PD&T for RPh Review Exception item to 9:30 AM 09/09 in QV

State Regulated Expiration Dates
If a state regulated rule exists (Regulatory Root Options #68 – 72, 294) for expiring an Rx and that Rx is eligible for Opioid to OTC offer: 
If the state regulated number of days to expire is less than 7 days, system shall use the ‘Rx Expired On’ expiration date (Refer to DE.01.68).
If the state regulated number of days to expire is 7 days or greater, the system shall use the calculated expiration date defined in DE.01.1984 #2.a.
System shall capture the Rx expiration date.

For Example:
Regulatory App Option #68 ‘Days from Date Written Specified to Set Expiration Date for CII Rx’ for state of AZ is set to 3 days.
If a CII drug is eligible for the opioid to OTC offer in the state of AZ; the Rx will be expired after 3 days based on Regulatory App Option #68 and not 7 days calculated for opioid to OTC offer.
